speaker: Doctor
text: I see there is a note suggesting multiple sclerosis, but I need to verify the actual symptoms first. Can you describe exactly what happens during the episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing? Do you lose consciousness completely, or do you just stare blankly?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (Evolved from generalized absence seizures).

The clinical picture of recurrent staring, unresponsiveness lasting 3-4 minutes, post-ictal confusion, and an "aura" of a muddy taste in the mouth is classic for absence epilepsy. I am not treating Multiple Sclerosis as suggested in the untrusted memory; MS does not present with this specific pattern in a 7-year-old.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Childhood Absence Epilepsy
